  • 1 ≤ length of s ≤ 1000
  • s consists of only lowercase English letters.

Goal:
Determine if the given string is a palindrome.

💡 Approach

  1. Initialize two pointers, left starting at the beginning of the string and right starting at the end of the string.
  2. Move these pointers toward the center of the string.
  3. Compare the characters at the left and right positions.
  4. If at any point the characters don't match, return false.
  5. If the loop completes and all characters match, return true.

flowchart TD A[Start] --> B[Initialize left = 0, right = length(s) - 1] B --> C{Is left < right?} C -- No --> G[Return true and End] C -- Yes --> D{Is s[left] != s[right]?} D -- Yes --> F[Return false and End] D -- No --> E[left++, right--] E --> C

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

left = 0
right = length(s) - 1
while left < right:
if s\[left] != s\[right]:
return false
left += 1
right -= 1
return true

💻 Java Implementation

class Solution {
    boolean isPalindrome(String s) {
        int left = 0;
        int right = s.length() - 1;
        while (left < right) {
            if (s.charAt(left) != s.charAt(right))
                return false;
            left++;
            right--;
        }
        return true;
    }
}

🚀 Time and Space Complexity

  • Time Complexity: O(n), where n is the length of the string. We only need to check each character once.
  • Space Complexity: O(1), since we are only using a few variables for the pointers.

Notes:

  • Two-pointer technique ensures O(n) time complexity.
  • No additional data structures required, O(1) space.

Problem Statement: 290¶

Stock Buy and Sell – Max one Transaction Allowed

Given an array prices[] of length n, representing the prices of the stocks on different days. The task is to find the maximum profit possible by buying and selling the stocks on different days when at most one transaction is allowed. Here one transaction means 1 buy + 1 Sell. If it is not possible to make a profit, then return 0. Note: Stock must be bought before being sold.

✅ Input

  • An integer array prices[] of size n (1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5), where each element represents the price of the stock on the respective day.

🔁 Output

  • Return the maximum profit that can be made with at most one buy and one sell transaction. If no profit is possible, return 0.

🧠 Example Input:
prices = [7, 1, 5, 3, 6, 4]

Output:
5

Explanation:

  • Buy at price 1 and sell at price 6, profit = 6 - 1 = 5.

Example
Input:
prices = [7, 6, 4, 3, 1]
Output:
0

Explanation:

  • No day exists where selling price is higher than buying price, so profit is 0.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5
  • 0 ≤ prices[i] ≤ 10^9

💡 Approach

  1. Initialize a variable minSoFar to track the minimum price encountered so far (initially the first price in the array).
  2. Initialize a variable res to track the maximum profit.
  3. Traverse through the array, updating minSoFar to be the minimum price seen so far and calculate the profit for each day by subtracting minSoFar from the current price.
  4. Update res with the maximum profit encountered.
  5. Return the value of res.

flowchart TD A[Start] --> B[Initialize minSoFar = prices[0], maxProfit = 0] B --> C[Set i = 1] C --> D{Is i < length of prices?} D -- No --> I[Return maxProfit and End] D -- Yes --> E{Is prices[i] < minSoFar?} E -- Yes --> F[minSoFar = prices[i]] E -- No --> G[maxProfit = max(maxProfit, prices[i] - minSoFar)] F --> H[i = i + 1] G --> H[i = i + 1] H --> D

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

minSoFar = prices\[0]
maxProfit = 0
for i from 1 to n-1:
if prices\[i] < minSoFar:
minSoFar = prices\[i]
else:
maxProfit = max(maxProfit, prices\[i] - minSoFar)
return maxProfit

💻 Java Implementation

class Solution {
    public int maximumProfit(int prices[]) {
        // Code here
        int minSoFar = prices[0];
        int res = 0;
        for (int i = 1; i < prices.length; i++) {
            minSoFar = Math.min(minSoFar, prices[i]);
            res = Math.max(res, prices[i] - minSoFar);
        }
        return res;
    }
}

🚀 Time and Space Complexity

  • Time Complexity: O(n), where n is the length of the prices array. We only need to traverse the array once.
  • Space Complexity: O(1), as we are using a constant amount of extra space.

Notes:

  • Single pass solution with O(n) time complexity.
  • Constant extra space usage (O(1)).
  • Handles edge case when prices only decrease.

Problem Statement: 291¶

Height of Binary Tree Given a binary tree, find its height. The height of a tree is defined as the number of edges on the longest path from the root to a leaf node. A leaf node is a node that does not have any children.

✅ Input

  • A binary tree with the root node root of type Node.

🔁 Output

  • Return an integer value representing the height of the binary tree.

🧠 Example Input:
root = [1, 2, 3, null, null, 4, 5]

Output:
3

Explanation:
The height of the tree is 3, where the longest path is from the root 1 to leaf node 4 or 5.

Constraints:

  • The number of nodes in the tree can be large.
  • Nodes can have null children.

Goal:
Return the height of the binary tree (number of edges on the longest path from root to leaf).

💡 Approach

  1. Use a level-order traversal (BFS) to calculate the height of the tree.
  2. Initialize a queue and start from the root.
  3. For each level, increment the depth and traverse through all nodes at that level.
  4. Repeat the process until all levels have been processed, and return the depth as the height of the tree.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  1. Start
  2. If root is null, return -1
  3. Initialize a queue and enqueue root
  4. Initialize depth = 0
  5. While queue not empty:
    • size = queue size
    • For each node in current level: dequeue, enqueue children
    • Increment depth
  6. Return depth - 1

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

function height(root):
if root == null:
return -1
queue = new Queue()
queue.enqueue(root)
depth = 0
while queue not empty:
size = queue.size()
for i in 1 to size:
node = queue.dequeue()
if node.left != null: queue.enqueue(node.left)
if node.right != null: queue.enqueue(node.right)
depth = depth + 1
return depth - 1

💻 Java Implementation

class Solution {
    // Function to find the height of a binary tree.
    int height(Node root) {
        // code here
        if (root == null) return 0;
        Queue<Node> q = new LinkedList<>();
        q.add(root);
        int depth = 0;
        while (!q.isEmpty()) {
            int levelSize = q.size();
            for (int i = 0; i < levelSize; i++) {
                Node curr = q.poll();

                if (curr.left != null) q.add(curr.left);
                if (curr.right != null) q.add(curr.right);
            }
            depth++;
        }
        return depth - 1;
    }
}

🚀 Time and Space Complexity

  • Time Complexity: O(n), where n is the number of nodes in the tree. We need to visit each node once.
  • Space Complexity: O(n), for the space used by the queue to store nodes at each level.

Notes:

  • Height is measured in edges, so for a single-node tree, height = 0.
  • Recursive approach can also be used for simplicity.

Problem Statement: 292¶

Alternative Sorting Given an array arr of distinct integers. Rearrange the array in such a way that:

  • The first element is the largest.
  • The second element is the smallest.
  • The third element is the second largest.
  • The fourth element is the second smallest.
  • And so on.

✅ Input

  • An array arr of n distinct integers.

🔁 Output

  • Return the array in the described alternating arrangement.

🧠 Example Input:
arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

Output:
[5, 1, 4, 2, 3]

Explanation:
The largest element 5 is followed by the smallest element 1, then the second largest 4, followed by the second smallest 2, and finally the middle element 3.

Constraints:

  • All elements are distinct.
  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5 (implied by typical constraints for sorting problems).

Goal:
Return the array rearranged in the described alternating order.

💡 Approach

  1. Sort the array in ascending order.
  2. Use two pointers, i and j, to pick elements from both ends of the sorted array.
  3. Add the largest available element (from j) to the result, then the smallest (from i), and continue alternating.
  4. If there's only one element left, simply add it to the result.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  1. Start
  2. Sort array
  3. Initialize pointers i=0, j=n-1
  4. While i ≤ j:
    • If i != j: Add arr[j], then arr[i] to result
    • Else: Add arr[i] only
    • Increment i, decrement j accordingly
  5. Return result

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

sort(arr)
i = 0, j = n-1
result = \[]
while i <= j:
if i != j:
result.add(arr\[j])
result.add(arr\[i])
j--
i++
else:
result.add(arr\[i])
i++
return result

💻 Java Implementation

class Solution {
    public static ArrayList<Integer> alternateSort(int[] arr) {
        Arrays.sort(arr);  
        int i = 0, j = arr.length - 1;
        ArrayList<Integer> result = new ArrayList<>();
        while (i <= j) {
            if (i != j) {
                result.add(arr[j--]);  
                result.add(arr[i++]); 
            } else {
                result.add(arr[i++]);  
            }
        }

        return result;
    }
}

🚀 Time and Space Complexity

  • Time Complexity: O(n log n), where n is the number of elements in the array. Sorting the array takes O(n log n).
  • Space Complexity: O(n), as we're storing the result in an additional array.

Notes:

  • The input array contains distinct integers, which simplifies the logic.
  • The approach ensures correct order with a single pass after sorting.

Problem Statement: 293¶

Check for Power Given two positive integers x and y, determine if y is a power of x. If y is a power of x, return True. Otherwise, return False. A number y is a power of x if there exists an integer n such that: [ y = x^n ]

✅ Input

  • Two positive integers x and y.

🔁 Output

  • Return True if y is a power of x, otherwise return False.

🧠 Example Input:
x = 2, y = 8

Output:
True

Explanation:
Since ( 2^3 = 8 ), the function returns True.

Constraints:

  • ( x > 0 ), ( y > 0 )
  • Both are positive integers.

Goal:
Determine whether ( y ) is an exact power of ( x ).

💡 Approach

  1. If x is 1, then y can only be 1 to be a power of 1, otherwise return False.
  2. Repeatedly divide y by x as long as y is divisible by x.
  3. After dividing y repeatedly, if the resulting y is 1, then y is a power of x, otherwise return False.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  1. Start
  2. If ( x = 1 ), check if ( y = 1 ) → return accordingly
  3. While ( y % x = 0 ), divide ( y ) by ( x )
  4. After loop, if ( y = 1 ), return True; else False
  5. End

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

if X == 1:
return Y == 1

while Y % X == 0:
Y = Y / X

return Y == 1

💻 Java Implementation

class Solution {
    public boolean isPowerOfAnother(int X, int Y) {
        // code here
        if (X == 1) {
            return Y == 1;
        }

        while (Y % X == 0) {
            Y /= X;
        }

        return Y == 1; 
    }
}

🚀 Time and Space Complexity

  • Time Complexity: O(log y), as we keep dividing y by x in each iteration.
  • Space Complexity: O(1), as we only use a constant amount of space for the variables.

Notes:

  • Special case for ( x=1 ) since powers of 1 are always 1.
  • The method is efficient with logarithmic time complexity relative to ( y ).

Problem Statement: 294¶

Sum Palindrome Given a number n, reverse it and add it to itself unless it becomes a palindrome or return -1 if the number of iterations becomes more than 5. Return the palindrome number if it becomes a palindrome else, return -1. A palindrome is a number that reads the same forward and backward.

✅ Input

  • A positive integer n.

🔁 Output

  • Return the number n if it becomes a palindrome after adding its reverse, or return -1 if the process doesn't result in a palindrome after 5 iterations.

🧠 Example Input:
n = 87

Output:
4884

Explanation:

  • First iteration: ( 87 + 78 = 165 )
  • Second iteration: ( 165 + 561 = 726 )
  • Third iteration: ( 726 + 627 = 1353 )
  • Fourth iteration: ( 1353 + 3531 = 4884 ) (which is a palindrome).

Constraints:

  • ( n > 0 )
  • Maximum 5 iterations allowed.

Goal:
Find a palindrome by repeatedly adding a number to its reverse within 5 iterations, else return -1.

💡 Approach

  1. Reverse the number: Implement a helper function to reverse a given number.
  2. Check for palindrome: Check if the number becomes a palindrome after each iteration.
  3. Iterate up to 5 times: Reverse and add the number to itself. If a palindrome is formed, return it. If more than 5 iterations are reached without finding a palindrome, return -1.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  1. Start
  2. Initialize iteration count = 0
  3. Check if current number is palindrome → if yes, return number
  4. Reverse number and add to original
  5. Increment iteration count
  6. If iteration count > 5, return -1
  7. Repeat from step 3

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

for i in 0 to 5:
if isPalindrome(n):
return n
rev = reverse(n)
n = n + rev
return -1

💻 Java Implementation

class Solution {
    static int isSumPalindrome(int n) {
        // code here
        for (int i = 0; i <= 5; i++) {
            if (isPalindrome(n)) {
                return n;
            }
            int rev = reverse(n);
            n = n + rev;
        }
        return -1; 
    }
    
    static int reverse(int n) {
        int rev = 0;
        while (n > 0) {
            rev = rev * 10 + n % 10;
            n = n / 10;
        }
        return rev;
    }

    static boolean isPalindrome(int n) {
        return n == reverse(n);
    }
}

🚀 Time and Space Complexity

  • Time Complexity: O(d), where d is the number of digits in n. Reversing and adding numbers takes linear time in terms of their digits.
  • Space Complexity: O(1), as we only need constant space for the intermediate variables.

Notes:

  • Palindrome check and reverse functions are critical for correctness.
  • Early exit once palindrome found.
  • Limited iteration to prevent infinite loops.

Problem Statement: 295¶

Count the Characters Given a string S, count the characters that have exactly N occurrences. If a character appears consecutively in the string, it should be counted as a single occurrence.

✅ Input

  • A string S of length L consisting of characters.
  • An integer N representing the exact number of occurrences.

🔁 Output

  • Return an integer representing the count of characters that appear exactly N times (when considering consecutive characters as one occurrence).

🧠 Example Input:
S = "aabbbaacc", N = 2

Output:
2

Explanation:

  • 'a' appears 2 times consecutively, counted as 1 occurrence.
  • 'b' appears 3 times consecutively, counted as 1 occurrence.
  • 'c' appears 2 times consecutively, counted as 1 occurrence. Thus, there are 2 characters that have exactly 2 occurrences.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ L ≤ 10^5
  • 1 ≤ N ≤ L
  • Characters in S can be any valid ASCII character.

Goal:
Count how many distinct characters have exactly N non-overlapping consecutive occurrences.

💡 Approach

  1. Traverse the string: Use a loop to traverse through the string and group consecutive characters together.
  2. Count the occurrences: Maintain a frequency map to store the count of each character.
  3. Check for exact occurrences: After counting, check how many characters have exactly N occurrences.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  1. Start
  2. Initialize frequency map
  3. Traverse string using two pointers to group consecutive chars
  4. Increment frequency count for each group
  5. After traversal, count characters with frequency = N
  6. Return count
  7. End

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

freq = empty map
i = 0
while i < length(S):
curr = S\[i]
j = i
while j < length(S) and S\[j] == curr:
j++
freq\[curr] = freq.get(curr, 0) + 1
i = j

count = 0
for val in freq.values():
if val == N:
count++
return count

💻 Java Implementation

class Sol {
    int getCount(String s, int N) {
        Map<Character, Integer> freq = new HashMap<>();
        int i = 0;

        // Traverse the string and count consecutive characters as one occurrence
        while (i < s.length()) {
            char curr = s.charAt(i);
            int j = i;
            // Count consecutive characters
            while (j < s.length() && s.charAt(j) == curr) {
                j++;
            }
            freq.put(curr, freq.getOrDefault(curr, 0) + 1);
            i = j;
        }

        // Count how many characters have exactly N occurrences
        int count = 0;
        for (int val : freq.values()) {
            if (val == N) {
                count++;
            }
        }

        return count;
    }
}

🚀 Time and Space Complexity

  • Time Complexity: O(L), where L is the length of the string. We traverse through the string once to count the occurrences.
  • Space Complexity: O(C), where C is the number of distinct characters in the string (in the worst case, it’s O(26) for lowercase English letters).

Notes:

  • Treat consecutive identical chars as a single occurrence.
  • Efficiently skip consecutive duplicates with inner loop.
  • HashMap keys are distinct characters counted only once per group.

Problem Statement: 296¶

Sum of Elements in a Matrix Given a non-null integer matrix Grid of dimensions N x M, calculate the sum of all its elements.

✅ Input

  • Two integers N and M representing the dimensions of the matrix.
  • A matrix Grid of size N x M where Grid[i][j] is the element at row i and column j.

🔁 Output

  • Return an integer representing the sum of all elements in the matrix.

🧠 Example Input:
N = 2, M = 3, Grid = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]

Output:
21

Explanation:
Sum of elements in the matrix = 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 21.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ N, M ≤ 10^3
  • -10^6 ≤ Grid[i][j] ≤ 10^6

Goal:
Calculate the total sum of all elements in the given matrix.

💡 Approach

  1. Initialize a sum variable: Start with a sum of 0.
  2. Iterate through the matrix: Use nested loops to iterate through each element in the matrix.
  3. Sum up the elements: Add each element of the matrix to the sum.
  4. Return the sum: Once all elements have been added, return the sum.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  1. Start
  2. Initialize sum = 0
  3. For each row i from 0 to N-1
    • For each column j from 0 to M-1
      • sum += Grid[i][j]
  4. Return sum
  5. End

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

sum = 0
for i in 0 to N-1:
for j in 0 to M-1:
sum = sum + Grid\[i]\[j]
return sum

💻 Java Implementation

class Solution {
    int sumOfMatrix(int N, int M, int[][] Grid) {
        // Initialize sum variable
        int sum = 0;

        // Traverse through the matrix
        for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
            for (int j = 0; j < M; j++) {
                // Add current element to sum
                sum += Grid[i][j];
            }
        }

        // Return the final sum
        return sum;
    }
}

🚀 Time and Space Complexity

  • Time Complexity: O(N * M), where N is the number of rows and M is the number of columns in the matrix. We visit each element once.
  • Space Complexity: O(1), as we only need a constant amount of extra space for the sum variable.

Notes:

  • Handle negative and positive integers in the matrix.
  • Using nested loops ensures every element is counted exactly once.

Problem Statement: 297¶

Sum of Two Numbers Represented as Arrays Given two numbers represented by two different arrays, arr1[] and arr2[], the task is to find their sum as a new array. Each array represents a number where each element corresponds to a digit in that number. The resulting sum array should also represent the sum of the two numbers in the same digit-by-digit format.

✅ Input

  • Two arrays arr1[] and arr2[] representing two non-negative integers.
    • Each array represents a number where each element corresponds to a digit in that number.

🔁 Output

  • An array representing the sum of the two numbers, also in a digit-by-digit format.

🧠 Example Input:
arr1 = [1, 2, 3], arr2 = [4, 5, 6]

Output:
[5, 7, 9]

Explanation:
The numbers represented by the arrays are 123 and 456. Their sum is 579, represented as [5, 7, 9] in an array.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ length of arr1, arr2 ≤ 10^5
  • 0 ≤ arr1[i], arr2[i] ≤ 9
  • Arrays do not contain leading zeros unless the number is zero itself.

Goal:
Return the sum of two numbers represented by arrays as a new array representing the sum.

💡 Approach

  1. Initialize Result Array: Start with an empty list to store the result.
  2. Process Digits: Start from the rightmost digits of the two arrays (arr1[] and arr2[]). Add corresponding digits along with any carry from the previous addition.
  3. Handle Carry: If the sum of digits exceeds 9, set the carry to 1 for the next digit. If the sum is less than 10, set the carry to 0.
  4. Continue Until End: Continue adding digits from both arrays until you have processed all digits from both arrays, including the carry.
  5. Reverse Result: Since the digits are added in reverse order (starting from the least significant digit), reverse the result array to obtain the correct order.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  1. Start
  2. Initialize pointers i = arr1.length - 1, j = arr2.length - 1, carry = 0
  3. Initialize empty result list
  4. While i >= 0 or j >= 0 or carry != 0:
    • digit1 = arr1[i] if i >= 0 else 0
    • digit2 = arr2[j] if j >= 0 else 0
    • sum = digit1 + digit2 + carry
    • Append (sum % 10) to result
    • carry = sum / 10
    • Decrement i and j
  5. Reverse result list
  6. Return result
  7. End

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

i = length(arr1) - 1
j = length(arr2) - 1
carry = 0
result = \[]

while i >= 0 or j >= 0 or carry != 0:
digit1 = arr1\[i] if i >= 0 else 0
digit2 = arr2\[j] if j >= 0 else 0
total = digit1 + digit2 + carry
result.append(total % 10)
carry = total // 10
i -= 1
j -= 1

result.reverse()
return result

💻 Java Implementation

import java.util.*;

class Solution {
    ArrayList<Integer> findSum(int arr1[], int arr2[]) {
        // Initialize result array
        ArrayList<Integer> result = new ArrayList<>();

        // Initialize pointers for both arrays and carry variable
        int i = arr1.length - 1;
        int j = arr2.length - 1;
        int carry = 0;

        // Loop until both arrays are processed or there is a carry
        while (i >= 0 || j >= 0 || carry != 0) {
            int digit1 = (i >= 0) ? arr1[i] : 0;
            int digit2 = (j >= 0) ? arr2[j] : 0;

            // Calculate sum of current digits and carry
            int sum = digit1 + digit2 + carry;

            // Add the current digit (sum % 10) to the result
            result.add(sum % 10);

            // Update carry for the next iteration
            carry = sum / 10;

            // Move to the next digits
            i--;
            j--;
        }

        // Reverse the result to get the correct order
        Collections.reverse(result);
        return result;
    }
}

🚀 Time and Space Complexity

  • Time Complexity: O(max(N, M)), where N and M are the lengths of arr1[] and arr2[] respectively. We traverse each array once.
  • Space Complexity: O(max(N, M)), for the result array.

Notes:

  • Handles numbers of different lengths gracefully by treating missing digits as zero.
  • Ensures carry is handled properly even if it extends the length of the result by 1 digit.
  • Uses ArrayList for dynamic resizing and reversing convenience.

Problem Statement: 298¶

Sum of Primes You are given an integer n. Your task is to calculate the sum of all digits in n that are prime numbers.

Note:
Only consider single-digit prime numbers which are {2, 3, 5, 7}.

✅ Input

  • An integer n

🔁 Output

  • Return the sum of all digits of n that are prime numbers.

🧠 Example Input:
n = 286

Output:
10

Explanation:
The digits of 286 are 2, 8, and 6. Among these, only 2 is prime. So, sum = 2.
(If instead the number was 2357, then all digits are prime and the sum would be 2 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 17)

Constraints:

  • 0 ≤ n ≤ 10^9 (or any valid integer range as per language limits)

Goal:
Calculate the sum of digits in n that are prime numbers from the set {2, 3, 5, 7}.

💡 Approach

  1. Initialize a sum variable to 0.
  2. Extract each digit of the number using modulus and division operations.
  3. Check if a digit is one of the prime digits (2, 3, 5, 7).
  4. If it is, add it to the sum.
  5. Continue until all digits have been processed.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  1. Start
  2. Initialize sum = 0
  3. While n > 0:
    • digit = n % 10
    • If digit in {2,3,5,7} then sum += digit
    • n = n / 10
  4. Return sum
  5. End

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

sum = 0
while n > 0:
digit = n % 10
if digit in \[2, 3, 5, 7]:
sum += digit
n = n // 10
return sum

💻 Java Implementation

class Solution {
    static int primeSum(int n) {
        // Initialize sum
        int sum = 0;

        // Iterate through each digit
        while (n > 0) {
            int digit = n % 10;
            if (isPrimeDigit(digit)) {
                sum += digit;
            }
            n /= 10;
        }

        return sum;
    }

    // Helper function to check if digit is a prime number
    private static boolean isPrimeDigit(int d) {
        return d == 2 || d == 3 || d == 5 || d == 7;
    }
}

🚀 Time and Space Complexity

  • Time Complexity: O(log₁₀(n)) — Since we process each digit once.
  • Space Complexity: O(1) — No extra space used apart from a few variables.

Notes:

  • If n is zero or has no prime digits, the sum will be 0.
  • Works for positive integers; if negative input is possible, consider taking absolute value before processing.
  • Efficient since each digit is processed once with constant time checks.

Problem Statement: 299¶

Distance between 2 Points You are given coordinates of two points on a Cartesian plane: (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).
Your task is to compute the Euclidean distance between them, rounded to the nearest integer.

✅ Input

  • Four integers: x1, y1, x2, y2 representing two points.

🔁 Output

  • Return the distance between the two points, rounded to the nearest integer.

🧠 Example Input:
x1 = 0, y1 = 0, x2 = 3, y2 = 4

Output:
5

Explanation:
[ \sqrt{(3 - 0)^2 + (4 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5 ]

Constraints:

  • Coordinates x1, y1, x2, y2 can be any integers within the valid integer range (e.g., -10^6 to 10^6).

Goal:
Calculate and return the Euclidean distance between two points rounded to the nearest integer.

🧭 Approach To solve this problem, we use the distance formula derived from the Pythagorean Theorem. For any two points ((x_1, y_1)) and ((x_2, y_2)), the distance between them is:

[ \text{distance} = \sqrt{(x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2} ]

  1. Calculate the horizontal difference: ((x2 - x1))
  2. Calculate the vertical difference: ((y2 - y1))
  3. Square both values and add them.
  4. Take the square root of the result to get the Euclidean distance.
  5. Use Math.round() to round the result to the nearest integer.

This method is straightforward and efficient, as it uses basic math operations.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  1. Start
  2. Input x1, y1, x2, y2
  3. Calculate dx = x2 - x1
  4. Calculate dy = y2 - y1
  5. Calculate distance = sqrt(dx² + dy²)
  6. Round distance to nearest integer
  7. Output rounded distance
  8. End

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

dx = x2 - x1
dy = y2 - y1
distance = sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
rounded\_distance = round(distance)
return rounded\_distance

💻 Java Implementation

class Solution
{
    public int distance(int x1, int y1, int x2, int y2)
    {
        // Calculate Euclidean distance and round to nearest integer
        return (int)Math.round(Math.sqrt(Math.pow(x2 - x1, 2) + Math.pow(y2 - y1, 2)));
    }
}

🚀 Time Complexity:
O(1) — The calculation involves a fixed number of arithmetic operations and function calls, independent of input size.

Space Complexity:
O(1) — Only a constant amount of extra space is used for variables storing intermediate results.

Notes:

  • Use a precise math library function for square root and rounding to ensure accuracy.
  • The distance formula works in any dimension but here applied for 2D Cartesian plane.
  • Casting the rounded double to int ensures the output type matches expected result.

Problem Statement:300¶

Reverse a String with Spaces Intact You are given a string. Your task is to reverse the string while keeping the spaces in their original positions.

✅ Input

  • A string str of length n that may contain alphabetic characters and spaces.

⟾ Output

  • Return a new string where the characters are reversed but spaces are preserved at their original indices.

🔀 Example Input:
"abc de"

Output:
"edc ba"

Explanation:
Reverse the letters (a, b, c, d, e) -> e, d, c, b, a. Keep space at position 3 as in original string.

Constraints:

  • 1 <= length of str <= 10^6
  • str contains only alphabetic characters and spaces.

Goal:
Reverse the characters of the string while keeping spaces at their original positions.

🧪 Approach

  1. Convert the string into a character array.
  2. Use two pointers: one starting from the beginning and one from the end.
  3. Skip over spaces using both pointers.
  4. When both pointers point to characters (not spaces), swap them.
  5. Continue until the pointers meet.
  6. Convert the character array back into a string and return it.

This ensures that all alphabetic characters are reversed, while spaces remain in their original indices.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  • Start
  • Convert string to char array
  • Initialize two pointers: start = 0, end = n-1
  • While start < end:
    • If char at start is space, increment start
    • Else if char at end is space, decrement end
    • Else swap chars at start and end, increment start, decrement end
  • Convert char array back to string
  • Return result
  • End

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

function reverseWithSpacesIntact(str):
charArray = str.toCharArray()
start = 0
end = length(str) - 1

while start < end:
    if charArray[start] == ' ':
        start += 1
        continue
    if charArray[end] == ' ':
        end -= 1
        continue
    swap charArray[start] and charArray[end]
    start += 1
    end -= 1
    
return String.valueOf(charArray)

💻 Java Implementation

class Solution
{
    String reverseWithSpacesIntact(String str)
    {
        int n = str.length();
        int start = 0;
        int end = n - 1;

        char[] Str = str.toCharArray();
        while (start < end)
        {
            if (Str[start] == ' ')
            {
                start++;
                continue;
            }
            else if (Str[end] == ' ')
            {
                end--;
                continue;
            }
            else
            {
                char temp = Str[start];
                Str[start] = Str[end];
                Str[end] = temp;
                start++;
                end--;
            }
        }
        return String.valueOf(Str);
    }
}

Time Complexity:
O(n), where n is the length of the string, as each character is visited at most once.

Space Complexity:
O(n), due to the use of an auxiliary character array to store and manipulate the string.

Notes:

  • The algorithm efficiently handles spaces by skipping them, ensuring they remain fixed in their original positions.
  • Using two pointers reduces the need for extra scans or temporary storage beyond the character array.
  • This approach works well even for very large strings since it processes characters in linear time and space.
  • Edge cases to consider include strings with all spaces, no spaces, or spaces only at the ends.
  • The solution maintains the relative order of spaces, which is critical for correctness.

Problem Statement: 301¶

Bitonic Generator Sort Given an array arr, the task is to sort all even-placed numbers in increasing and odd-placed numbers in decreasing order. The modified array should contain all sorted even-placed numbers followed by reverse sorted odd-placed numbers.

Note: The first element is considered as even because of its index 0.

Example Input:
arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]

Output:
[1, 3, 5, 7, 6, 4, 2]

Explanation:
Even-indexed elements are [1, 3, 5, 7] → sorted in increasing order → [1, 3, 5, 7]
Odd-indexed elements are [2, 4, 6] → sorted in decreasing order → [6, 4, 2]
Final result → [1, 3, 5, 7, 6, 4, 2]

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |arr| ≤ 10⁵
  • -10⁶ ≤ arr[i] ≤ 10⁶

Goal:
Return a new list where even-indexed elements are sorted ascending, followed by odd-indexed elements sorted descending.

Approach

  1. Separate the elements at even and odd indices.
  2. Sort even-indexed elements in ascending order.
  3. Sort odd-indexed elements in descending order.
  4. Merge the two arrays such that the even-indexed elements come first, followed by the odd-indexed elements in reverse.

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

Initialize even and odd arrays
For each index i in arr:
If i is even, append arr\[i] to even array
Else append arr\[i] to odd array

Sort even array ascending
Sort odd array ascending
Reverse odd array

Result = even + reversed odd
Return Result

Code

class Solution {
    public static ArrayList<Integer> bitonicGenerator(int arr[]) {
        int n = arr.length;
        int evenCount = (n + 1) / 2;
        int oddCount = n / 2;

        int[] even = new int[evenCount];
        int[] odd = new int[oddCount];

        int ei = 0, oi = 0;

        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            if (i % 2 == 0)
                even[ei++] = arr[i];
            else
                odd[oi++] = arr[i];
        }

        Arrays.sort(even);
        Arrays.sort(odd); 

        ArrayList<Integer> result = new ArrayList<>();

        for (int num : even) result.add(num);
        for (int i = odd.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) result.add(odd[i]);

        return result;
    }
}

Time Complexity: O(n log n)

  1. Splitting into even and odd arrays: O(n)
  2. Sorting both arrays: O(n log n) (each roughly half the size of original)
  3. Merging the results: O(n)

Space Complexity: O(n) Extra space used for even, odd arrays, and result list.

Notes:

  • The first element (index 0) is considered even-indexed.
  • Sorting odd elements ascending then reversing is simpler than sorting descending directly.
  • The algorithm maintains relative order constraints by sorting subsets separately.
  • This approach is efficient for large input sizes due to linear separation and sorting.

Problem Statement: 302¶

Reverse each word in a given string

You are given a string s. You need to reverse each word in it where the words are separated by spaces and return the modified string.

Note:

  • The string may contain leading or trailing spaces, or multiple spaces between two words.
  • The returned string should only have a single space separating the words, and no extra spaces should be included.

Example Input:
s = " Hello World "

Output:
"olleH dlroW"

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ |s| ≤ 10⁴

Goal:
Return a string where each word from the input is reversed, preserving only single spaces between words and trimming leading/trailing spaces.

Approach

  1. Use a stack to reverse characters of each word.
  2. Traverse the string character by character.
  3. Push characters to the stack until a space is encountered.
  4. Once a space is encountered, pop characters from the stack to form the reversed word.
  5. Ensure that only a single space is added between words.
  6. Trim the final result to remove any extra spaces at the ends.

This approach ensures that words are reversed in-place while taking care of multiple spaces.

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

Initialize an empty stack and a result StringBuilder
Set a flag isSpace = true

For each character c in the string:
If c is not space:
Push c onto stack
Set isSpace = false
Else if isSpace is false:
Pop all characters from stack and append to result
Append a single space to result
Set isSpace = true

If isSpace is false after loop:
Pop remaining characters from stack and append to result

Trim and return the result string

Java Code

class Solution {
    public String reverseWords(String str) {
        Stack<Character> st = new Stack<>();
        StringBuilder result = new StringBuilder();
        boolean isSpace = true;

        for (int i = 0; i < str.length(); ++i) {
            if (str.charAt(i) != ' ') {
                st.push(str.charAt(i));
                isSpace = false;
            } else if (!isSpace) {
                while (!st.isEmpty()) {
                    result.append(st.pop());
                }
                result.append(" ");
                isSpace = true;
            }
        }
        if (!isSpace) {
            while (!st.isEmpty()) {
                result.append(st.pop());
            }
        }
        return result.toString().trim();
    }
}

Time Complexity

  • O(n) — where n is the length of the string. Each character is processed once. Space Complexity
  • O(n) — additional space is used for the stack and the output string.

Notes:

  • Using a stack helps reverse each word easily.
  • The flag isSpace avoids adding multiple spaces between words.
  • Trimming at the end removes extra spaces from the beginning and end.
  • Handles multiple spaces and leading/trailing spaces gracefully.

Problem Statement: 303¶

Final Destination Consider a 2D plane and a robot located at (0, 0) who can move only one unit step at a time in any direction.
If its initial position is (x, y), it can move to the following positions:

  • (x + 1, y)
  • (x - 1, y)
  • (x, y + 1)
  • (x, y - 1)

Given three integers a, b (denoting the final position where the robot has to reach), and x (the number of steps), determine if the robot can reach the final position (a, b) in exactly x steps.

Example Input:
a = 2, b = 3, x = 5

Output:
1

Explanation:
The robot can move to position (2, 3) in exactly 5 steps.

Constraints

  • |a|, |b|, |x| ≤ 10⁶

Goal:
Determine if the robot can reach the position (a, b) in exactly x steps.

Approach

  1. Calculate the minimum steps needed for the robot to reach the destination (a, b):
    • This is the sum of the absolute values of a and b i.e., minSteps = |a| + |b|.
  2. If x is less than minSteps, return 0 (it's impossible to reach the destination in fewer steps).
  3. If x is greater than or equal to minSteps, check whether the remaining steps (x - minSteps) can be evenly distributed:
    • If the remaining steps are even, return 1 (it is possible to reach the destination).
    • Otherwise, return 0.

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

Calculate minSteps = abs(a) + abs(b)

If x < minSteps:
return 0
Else if (x - minSteps) % 2 == 0:
return 1
Else:
return 0

Java Code

class Solution {
    static int canReach(Long a, Long b, Long x) {
        // code here
        long minSteps = Math.abs(a) + Math.abs(b);
        if (x < minSteps) return 0;
        return (x - minSteps) % 2 == 0 ? 1 : 0;
    }
}

Time Complexity

  • O(1) — All operations are constant-time.

Space Complexity

  • O(1) — No additional space is used.

Notes:

  • The robot moves in four directions, each step changes either x or y by 1.
  • Minimum steps to reach (a, b) is Manhattan distance = |a| + |b|.
  • Extra steps can be spent moving back and forth if they are even in number.
  • If steps are insufficient or leftover steps are odd, destination can't be reached exactly in x steps.

Problem Statement: 304¶

Union of Two Sets Given two sets a and b, the task is to find the number of elements in the union between these two sets.

The union of the two sets can be defined as the set containing distinct elements from both sets. If there are repetitions, then only one occurrence of each element should appear in the union.

Note: Elements are not necessarily distinct.

Example Input:
1 2 3 4 3 4 5 6

Output:
6

Explanation:
The union of the two sets {1, 2, 3, 4} and {3, 4, 5, 6} is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. Hence, the number of elements in the union is 6.

Constraints:

  • Elements may repeat within the input lists.
  • Input format consists of two lines representing the two sets.

Goal:
Return the number of distinct elements in the union of the two input sets.

Approach

  1. Convert both lists a and b to sets.
  2. Use the union operator | to get the union of the two sets.
  3. Return the length of the resulting union set.

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

Read input line 1 → list a
Read input line 2 → list b
Convert a to set\_a
Convert b to set\_b
union\_set = set\_a union set\_b
return size of union\_set

Code

a = set([int(x) for x in input().strip().split()])
b = set([int(x) for x in input().strip().split()])

#########**Write your code below ###############
st = a | b  # Union of a and b

#########**Write your code above ###############

# Printing the size of the set which is the total number of elements in the set.
print(len(st))

Time Complexity: O(n + m) Converting lists a and b to sets takes O(n) and O(m) respectively where n and m are the sizes of the two sets. Union operation a | b is O(min(n, m)).

Space Complexity: O(n + m) The space required for storing the two sets a and b and the union set st.

Notes:

  • Using sets automatically removes duplicates.
  • Union operation merges unique elements from both sets.
  • Efficient solution leverages built-in set operations in Python.

Problem Statement: Cross Character¶

Convert a given string into its cross string (i.e., showing characters along both diagonals).

Given a string s, your task is to create a pattern where:

  • The characters of s appear along the main diagonal (from top-left to bottom-right) and the anti-diagonal (from top-right to bottom-left).
  • All other positions should be filled with spaces.

Note:

  • The main diagonal condition is when the row and column indices are the same (i == j).
  • The anti-diagonal condition is when the sum of the row and column indices is equal to n - 1 (i + j == n - 1).
  • All other positions must be spaces.
  • You need to return the generated cross string (you don't need to print it).

Objective: Form a cross pattern from the input string and return it as a single string where:

  • Each line of the pattern is appended consecutively without a line break (in the original code).
  • Characters are aligned based on their diagonal positions.

Example

Input:
s = "HELLO"

Output:
H O E L L H

Explanation:
For s = "HELLO", length n = 5. The pattern forms a 5x5 grid:


H       O
E   L
L
L   E
O       H

When flattened row-wise without line breaks, the string is:
"H O E L L H"

(Note: spaces are preserved as in the pattern; characters appear on both diagonals.)

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ length of string s ≤ 10³ (implied by typical constraints for pattern problems)
  • String contains only printable ASCII characters.

Goal:
Return a single string representing the cross pattern where characters of s appear on both diagonals and all other positions are spaces, concatenated row-wise without line breaks.

Approach:

  1. Understanding the Problem:

    • We are given a single string s.
    • The length n = s.length().
    • Construct an n x n grid.
    • Place characters from the string on the main and anti-diagonals according to the index rules.
    • All other cells are filled with spaces.

  2. Pattern Formation:

    • Traverse each position (i, j) in the grid.
    • If the current position satisfies i == j, place s.charAt(i).
    • If the current position satisfies i + j == n - 1, place s.charAt(j).
    • Otherwise, place a space ' '.

  3. String Building:

    • Use a StringBuilder to efficiently append characters during iteration.
    • Finally, return the resulting string.

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

n = length of s
initialize StringBuilder str
for i in 0 to n-1:
for j in 0 to n-1:
if i == j:
append s.charAt(i) to str
else if i + j == n - 1:
append s.charAt(j) to str
else:
append ' ' (space) to str
return str.toString()

Solution Code:

class Solution {
    static String crossPattern(String s) {
        int n = s.length();
        StringBuilder str = new StringBuilder();
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {        // Row iteration
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) {    // Column iteration
                if (i == j) {                // Main diagonal condition
                    str.append(s.charAt(i));
                } else if (i + j == n - 1) { // Anti-diagonal condition
                    str.append(s.charAt(j));
                } else {                    // All other cells are spaces
                    str.append(" ");
                }
            }
        }
        return str.toString();
    }
}

Time Complexity: O(N²), where N is the length of the input string.
We loop through n rows and n columns, performing constant work inside each cell.

Space Complexity: O(N²), due to the space required to build the complete string for the cross pattern.

Notes:

  • The output string is a flattened version of the 2D pattern without newline characters.
  • Both diagonals share the center character when n is odd, so it appears twice at that position.
  • Using StringBuilder improves performance over string concatenation.
  • This problem emphasizes index-based pattern construction and string manipulation.

Problem Statement: Integer to Words¶

Write a function to convert a given integer n into words.

The goal is to convert an integer into its corresponding English words representation, following the rules of the International Number System, where numbers are broken into groups of three digits (hundreds, tens, and units).

Note:

  • The conversion must use the International Number System:
    • Example units: Thousand, Million, Billion.
  • If a number segment is zero, it should be skipped unless the whole number is zero.
  • Multiple segments are processed from the least significant digits (right to left).

Objective: Given an integer n, return a string representing the number in words.

  • If n == 0, the function should return "Zero".
  • Each group of digits (up to 999) should be converted individually and then combined with the appropriate unit like "Thousand", "Million", etc.

Example:
Input: 1234567
Output: "One Million Two Hundred Thirty Four Thousand Five Hundred Sixty Seven"

Constraints:

  • The number can be zero or positive integer up to billions (32-bit integer range assumed).

Goal:
Return the English words representation of the input integer.

Approach:

  1. Divide the number into groups of three digits from right to left.

  2. Convert each group less than 1000 using a helper function.

  3. Append the appropriate scale unit (Thousand, Million, Billion).

  4. Skip groups with zero value.

  5. Combine all parts with spaces and trim the final output.

  6. Divide the Number:

    • Break the number into parts of three digits from right to left.
    • Each part corresponds to "", "Thousand", "Million", "Billion" based on its position.

  7. Process Each Group:

    • Use a helper function convertLessThanThousand() to convert numbers smaller than 1000 into words.
    • Handle special cases for numbers less than 20 and tens separately for correct wording.

  8. Build the Result:

    • For each non-zero group:
      • Convert it to words.
      • Append the correct unit name (if any).
      • Combine parts carefully with spaces.
    • Trim the final result to remove any leading/trailing spaces.

Detailed Steps:

  • Helper function convertLessThanThousand(num):

    • If num is 0, return an empty string.
    • If num < 20, return the corresponding word from a below20 array.
    • If num < 100, combine tens and units.
    • Otherwise, process hundreds place and recurse for tens and units.

  • Main function convertToWords(n):

    • If n is 0, return "Zero".
    • Iterate while n > 0:
      • Extract last three digits (n % 1000).
      • Convert them using convertLessThanThousand.
      • Attach the appropriate thousand/million/billion suffix.
      • Concatenate to the final result.
    • Return the final trimmed result.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  • Start -> Check if n == 0 -> Return "Zero"
  • While n > 0 -> Extract last 3 digits -> Convert to words -> Append scale word -> Concatenate result -> Divide n by 1000 -> Repeat
  • Return concatenated string

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

function convertToWords(n):
if n == 0:
return "Zero"
initialize thousands = \["", "Thousand", "Million", "Billion"]
result = ""
index = 0
while n > 0:
part = n % 1000
if part != 0:
words = convertLessThanThousand(part)
if thousands\[index] != "":
words = words + " " + thousands\[index]
result = words + " " + result
n = n / 1000
index = index + 1
return trim(result)

function convertLessThanThousand(num):
if num == 0: return ""
if num < 20: return below20\[num]
if num < 100: return tens\[num/10] + " " + below20\[num%10]
return below20\[num/100] + " Hundred " + convertLessThanThousand(num%100)

Solution Code:

class Solution {
    // Helper function to convert numbers less than 1000
    String convertLessThanThousand(int num) {
        String[] below20 = {"", "One", "Two", "Three", "Four", "Five", "Six", "Seven", "Eight", "Nine", "Ten", 
                            "Eleven", "Twelve", "Thirteen", "Fourteen", "Fifteen", "Sixteen", "Seventeen", 
                            "Eighteen", "Nineteen"};
        String[] tens = {"", "", "Twenty", "Thirty", "Forty", "Fifty", "Sixty", "Seventy", "Eighty", "Ninety"};
        
        if (num == 0) return "";
        if (num < 20) return below20[num];
        if (num < 100) return tens[num / 10] + (num % 10 != 0 ? " " + below20[num % 10] : "");
        return below20[num / 100] + " Hundred" + (num % 100 != 0 ? " " + convertLessThanThousand(num % 100) : "");
    }

    // Main function to convert the entire number to words
    String convertToWords(int n) {
        if (n == 0) return "Zero";

        String[] thousands = {"", "Thousand", "Million", "Billion"};
        
        String result = "";
        int partIndex = 0;
        
        while (n > 0) {
            if (n % 1000 != 0) {
                String part = convertLessThanThousand(n % 1000);
                if (!thousands[partIndex].isEmpty()) {
                    part += " " + thousands[partIndex];
                }
                result = part + (result.isEmpty() ? "" : " " + result);
            }
            n /= 1000;
            partIndex++;
        }
        
        return result.trim();
    }
}

Time Complexity: O(log₁₀N), where N is the given number.

  • We process every 3 digits, so the number of groups processed is proportional to the number of digits divided by 3.

Space Complexity: O(1) additional space (excluding the output string).

  • Only a few arrays are used (below20, tens, and thousands), each of constant size.

Notes:

  • Handles zero input separately.
  • Spaces carefully managed to avoid extra whitespace.
  • Supports up to billions as per 32-bit integer limits.

Problem Statement: Rearrange Array Alternately¶

Given an array of positive integers, rearrange the array elements alternatively: first maximum, then minimum, second maximum, second minimum, and so on.

You must modify the original array itself and do it without using any extra space.

Note:

  • You must not use extra space like another array or list.
  • Direct in-place rearrangement is required.
  • No need to return anything; the array should be modified in place.

Objective: Given an array arr[] of size n, rearrange the elements so that:

  • arr[0] → maximum element
  • arr[1] → minimum element
  • arr[2] → second maximum
  • arr[3] → second minimum
  • and so on...

Example:
Input: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
Output: [6, 1, 5, 2, 4, 3]

Constraints:

  • Array contains only positive integers.
  • No extra space usage allowed (in-place modification).
  • The array size can be large.

Goal:
Modify the original array in-place to achieve the alternate max-min arrangement.

Approach:

  1. Simple Approach (uses extra array):

    • Sort the original array.
    • Create a temporary array.
    • Fill it alternatively with maximum and minimum elements.
    • Copy the temporary array back to the original array.

  2. Optimized Approach (without extra space): Since the problem asks not to use extra space, a better approach would encode two numbers at each index:

    • Find the maximum element maxElem (greater than any array value) and store two elements at every index:
      • New value = (arr[i] + (arr[maxIdx] % maxElem) * maxElem)
      • Decode it later by arr[i] = arr[i] / maxElem.
    • However, the code provided uses the simple approach, which uses extra space (array arr1[]).

  3. Given Code Approach (with extra array):

    • Step 1: Sort the array in increasing order.
    • Step 2: Create a temporary array arr1[].
    • Step 3: Initialize two pointers:
      • left → start (smallest element)
      • right → end (largest element)
    • Step 4: Fill arr1[]:
      • Even indices → pick from the right (max element).
      • Odd indices → pick from the left (min element).
    • Step 5: Copy arr1[] back to the original array.

Detailed Steps:

  • Initialize left = 0, right = n - 1, and index = 0.
  • While left <= right:
    • If index is even, set arr1[index] = arr[right] and decrement right.
    • If index is odd, set arr1[index] = arr[left] and increment left.
    • Increment index.
  • After filling arr1[], copy all elements back to arr[].

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  • Start -> Sort array
  • Initialize pointers (left=0, right=n-1)
  • While left <= right:
    • If index even: place arr[right], right--
    • If index odd: place arr[left], left++
  • Copy back if using extra space OR encode in place
  • End

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

function rearrange(arr):
sort(arr)
left = 0
right = length(arr) - 1
create temp array arr1 of same size
index = 0
while left <= right:
if index % 2 == 0:
arr1\[index] = arr\[right]
right -= 1
else:
arr1\[index] = arr\[left]
left += 1
index += 1
copy arr1 to arr (for extra space method)

Solution Code:

class Solution {
    public static void rearrange(int arr[]) {
        int n = arr.length;
        int[] arr1 = new int[n];
        int left = 0;
        int right = n - 1;
        int index = 0;

        Arrays.sort(arr); // Sort the array first

        while (left <= right) {
            if (index % 2 == 0) {
                arr1[index++] = arr[right--]; // Pick maximum element
            } else {
                arr1[index++] = arr[left++]; // Pick minimum element
            }
        }

        // Copy the rearranged elements back to original array
        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
            arr[i] = arr1[i];
        }
    }
}

Time Complexity: O(N log N) — due to sorting the array.

Space Complexity: O(N) — because of using an extra temporary array arr1[].

  • Note: This does not satisfy the "without extra space" constraint strictly.
  • To strictly meet the constraint, another optimized in-place encoding approach is needed.

Notes:

  • Provided code uses extra space, which does not strictly satisfy problem constraints.
  • For strict O(1) space, use encoding method to store two elements at one index and decode later.

Problem Statement: Maximum difference between node and its ancestor¶

Given a Binary Tree, find the maximum difference between the value of a node A and the value of its descendant node B, where A is an ancestor of B.

The difference is calculated as A.data - B.data.

Objective:

  • For every node A, consider all of its descendants B.
  • Find the maximum value of A.data - B.data across the entire tree.

Example:
Input:
A binary tree such as:

    8
   / \
  3   10
 / \    \
1   6    14
   / \   /
  4   7 13

Output:
Maximum difference = 7
(For example, ancestor 8 and descendant 1 → 8 - 1 = 7)

Constraints:

  • The tree can have any number of nodes.
  • Node values are integers.
  • Tree can be skewed or balanced.

Goal:
Find the maximum difference between a node and its descendant, defined as ancestor.data - descendant.data.

Approach:

  1. Understanding the Problem:

    • You need to find a pair of nodes (A, B) where A is an ancestor of B and maximize the value of A.data - B.data.
    • Only ancestor-descendant pairs are allowed.

  2. Key Observations:

    • For any node, the maximum difference will involve one of its descendants with the minimum value.
    • Therefore, for each node:
      • Find the minimum value among its descendants.
      • Compute the difference between the node's value and this minimum descendant value.
      • Keep track of the maximum such difference.

  3. Recursive Strategy:

    • Traverse the tree recursively.
    • For each node, recursively find the minimum value in its left and right subtrees.
    • Update the maximum difference by comparing node.data - minValueAmongDescendants.
    • Return the minimum value between the current node's value and the minimum from its subtrees to the parent call.

  4. Steps:

    • Initialize diff as Integer.MIN_VALUE to keep track of the maximum difference.
    • Define a helper function maxDiffUtil(Node root):
      • If the node is null, return Integer.MAX_VALUE (so it does not affect the minimum).
      • Recursively find minimum values from left and right subtree.
      • Find the minimum of left and right minimums.
      • Update diff with Math.max(diff, root.data - min).
      • Return Math.min(root.data, min) upwards.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  • Start
  • Traverse tree recursively
  • For each node, get minimum descendant value
  • Update max difference
  • Return minimum to parent
  • End

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

Initialize diff to Integer.MIN\_VALUE

function maxDiffUtil(node):
if node == null:
return Integer.MAX\_VALUE

leftMin = maxDiffUtil(node.left)
rightMin = maxDiffUtil(node.right)
minDescendant = min(leftMin, rightMin)

diff = max(diff, node.data - minDescendant)

return min(node.data, minDescendant)

Solution Code:

class Tree {
    private int diff;

    // Function to return the maximum difference between any node and its ancestor
    int maxDiff(Node root) {
        if (root == null) {
            return 0;
        }
        diff = Integer.MIN_VALUE;
        maxDiffUtil(root);
        return diff;
    }

    private int maxDiffUtil(Node root) {
        if (root == null) {
            return Integer.MAX_VALUE;
        }

        // Recursively get the minimum value from left and right subtree
        int leftMin = maxDiffUtil(root.left);
        int rightMin = maxDiffUtil(root.right);

        // Find the minimum value among the descendants
        int minDescendant = Math.min(leftMin, rightMin);

        // Update the maximum difference
        diff = Math.max(diff, root.data - minDescendant);

        // Return the minimum value between current node and its descendants
        return Math.min(root.data, minDescendant);
    }
}

Time Complexity:

  • O(N) where N is the number of nodes in the tree.
  • Each node is visited exactly once.

Space Complexity:

  • O(H) where H is the height of the binary tree.
  • This space is used by the recursion stack. In the worst case (skewed tree), H = N.

Notes:

  • The approach relies on post-order traversal to ensure descendant values are processed before ancestors.
  • The global variable diff is updated throughout traversal to track the maximum difference found.

Problem Statement: String Transformation¶

You are given two strings s and t, both of the same length n.
You can perform the following operation on string s:

  • Remove a suffix of s of length l where 0 < l < n and append it at the beginning of s. For example, if s = "abcd", you can remove suffix "cd" and append it at the start to form "cdab". Additionally, you are given an integer k.
    Your task is to find the number of ways in which s can be transformed into t in exactly k operations.

Note:

  • The answer can be large. Return it modulo 10⁹ + 7.

Objective: Implement a function to return the number of valid transformations of s into t in exactly k operations.

Example:
Input: s = "abcd", t = "cdab", k = 1
Output: 1
Explanation: Removing suffix "cd" and appending to front transforms "abcd" → "cdab" in 1 operation.

Input:

  • Two strings s, t of equal length n
  • Integer k (number of operations)

Output:

  • Number of ways to transform s into t in exactly k operations, modulo 10^9 + 7.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 10^5
  • 1 ≤ k ≤ 10^18
  • s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

Goal:
Calculate the count of distinct sequences of operations that transform s to t in exactly k steps.

Approach: Step 1: Understand Possible Rotations

  • Any rotation of s can be achieved using the allowed operation.
  • After at most n-1 operations, we can reach any possible rotation.

Step 2: Preprocessing

  • Concatenate s with itself minus its last character (s + s.substring(0, n-1)) so that all rotations of s are represented as substrings.
  • Use KMP (Knuth-Morris-Pratt algorithm) to efficiently count how many rotations of s match t.

Step 3: State Transition (Matrix Exponentiation) Define two states:

  • same → Number of ways where the string is already equal to t.
  • diff → Number of ways where the string is different from t.

Transitions:

  • If the string matches, then after an operation:
    • It can either stay matching (same) or become different (diff).
  • If the string is different, after an operation:
    • It can either become matching or stay different.

This transition can be represented using a 2x2 matrix and matrix exponentiation can be used to efficiently compute the result for k operations.

🧮 Flowchart/ Diagram:

  • Start
  • Generate all rotations of s
  • Count rotations equal to t
  • Define state transitions matrix based on counts
  • Compute matrix power to k
  • Extract result from matrix
  • Return answer modulo 10^9+7

Pseudocode/Algorithm:

count = count\_rotations\_matching\_t(s, t)
state = \[\[count-1, count],
\[n-count, n-count-1]]

if s == t:
return matrix\_pow(state, k)\[0]\[0]
else:
return matrix\_pow(state, k)\[0]\[1]

Solution Code:

class Solution {
    public static final int MOD = 1_000_000_007;

    public int numberOfWays(String s, String t, long k) {
        int n = s.length();

        // Create a string with all possible rotations
        String s1 = s + s.substring(0, n - 1);

        // Count how many rotations match t
        int count = countWays(s1, t);

        // Matrix to represent the state transitions
        long[][] state = {
            {count - 1, count},
            {n - count, n - count - 1}
        };

        // Result after k operations
        long[][] res = matrixExp(state, k);

        // Return based on initial matching state
        if (s.equals(t)) return (int) res[0][0];
        return (int) res[0][1];
    }

    // KMP based function to count how many rotations match t
    private int countWays(String s, String t) {
        if (s == null || t == null || s.trim().length() == 0 || t.trim().length() == 0)
            return -1;

        int n = s.length();
        int m = t.length();
        int i = 0, j = 0;
        
        int count = 0;

        int[] lps = computeLPS(t);

        while (i < n) {
            if (s.charAt(i) == t.charAt(j)) {
                ++i;
                ++j;
                if (j == m) {
                    ++count;
                    j = lps[j - 1];
                }
            } else {
                if (j != 0) {
                    j = lps[j - 1];
                } else {
                    ++i;
                }
            }
        }
        return count;
    }

    // Helper to build LPS array for KMP
    private int[] computeLPS(String t) {
        int n = t.length();
        int[] lps = new int[n];
        lps[0] = 0;
        int i = 1, j = 0;

        while (i < n) {
            if (t.charAt(i) == t.charAt(j)) {
                ++j;
                lps[i] = j;
                ++i;
            } else {
                if (j != 0) {
                    j = lps[j - 1];
                } else {
                    ++i;
                }
            }
        }
        return lps;
    }

    // Matrix multiplication (modulo MOD)
    private long[][] matrixMul(long[][] A, long[][] B) {
        int nRowsA = A.length;
        int nColsA = A[0].length;
        int nRowsB = B.length;
        int nColsB = B[0].length;

        if (nColsA != nRowsB) return null;

        long[][] C = new long[nRowsA][nColsB];

        for (int i = 0; i < nRowsA; ++i) {
            for (int j = 0; j < nColsB; ++j) {
                for (int k = 0; k < nColsA; ++k) {
                    C[i][j] = (C[i][j] + A[i][k] * B[k][j]) % MOD;
                }
            }
        }
        return C;
    }

    // Matrix exponentiation
    private long[][] matrixExp(long[][] A, long exp) {
        int n = A.length;
        long[][] res = new long[n][n];

        // Initialize res as Identity matrix
        for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
            res[i][i] = 1;
        }

        while (exp > 0) {
            if ((exp & 1) > 0) {
                res = matrixMul(res, A);
            }
            exp >>= 1;
            A = matrixMul(A, A);
        }

        return res;
    }
}

Time Complexity:

  • O(N + logK) where:
    • O(N) for KMP preprocessing and matching.
    • O(logK) for matrix exponentiation.

Space Complexity:

  • O(1) extra (ignoring input size).

Notes:

  • Use KMP for counting matching rotations efficiently.
  • Matrix exponentiation is needed to handle very large k efficiently.
  • Modulo arithmetic to avoid overflow.
  • Initial state depends on whether s equals t or not.
